AON IS IN THE BUSINESS OF BETTER DECISIONS

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are committed as one firm to our purpose, united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

About The Role

AI has made our developers fast. How quickly we deliver now depends on how well the work is defined, and this role is where that happens.

You'll own the application from start to finish, as the business's trusted partner and main point of contact. You'll also lead the team that builds what they need. Our business partners are experts in their field with full schedules, so they often share requests in brief. You'll understand the need behind each request, ask the questions that bring out the full picture, and deliver something better than they expected, quickly.

This is a hands-on, blended role: mostly business analyst, plus product manager, designer, tester and technical problem-solver. You'll do the work yourself, from discovery and design to story creation and testing, and lead the team by example. You'll work closely with US-based business and consulting teams who have not worked with an offshore development team before, so building trust quickly matters. You'll have a handover period working directly with the current product owner.

How You Operate

You're a partner, not an order-taker. You form your own view, bring recommendations, and use your judgment when something doesn't add up.
You take the burden off the business. If they would otherwise enter data by hand, you offer to load it. If their data isn't clean, you work through it instead of sending it back. You know their work well enough to make the everyday design calls yourself, so they're only pulled in for the decisions that truly need them. You anticipate needs and deliver more than they asked for.
You push AI further than others do. Here, AI isn't an add-on, it's how the work gets done. You're empowered to experiment boldly, keep raising the bar on what it can deliver, and move at a speed that wouldn't be possible without it.
You build what you'd want to use. If something is confusing or clunky, you won't accept it, even if it technically meets the requirement.
You own quality. You wrote the story, so you're the best person to confirm it does what the business intended.
You're a trusted source. You move fast, and when you say something is handled, it is.

What You'll Do

Lead the business relationship

Be the primary contact for new development, enhancements and production issues, and own issues from report to resolution.
Lead demos, handle questions with confidence, and turn feedback into next steps.

Shape and define the work

Lead discovery with busy stakeholders, read between the lines, and turn early ideas into a defined scope.
Recommend what to build and what not to build, and break large initiatives into small, testable phases.
Write user stories with detailed acceptance criteria (Gherkin preferred) that developers and AI coding tools can build from without guessing.
Use AI across the whole workflow: discovery prep, stories, prototypes, and data work. Turn what works into reusable approaches for the team.

Design and test for the user

Keep end users at the center of every decision.
Use AI to build prototypes and settle the design before development starts.
Test every delivered story against its scenarios, and work with the automation QA engineer so the automated scripts cover them.

Work hands-on with data

Use SQL to analyze data, reconcile inconsistent source files, prepare safe, repeatable data loads, and check results against the source of truth.

Lead the team

Set priorities, unblock developers, and make sure the team understands why it's building what it's building.
Run backlog grooming, story acceptance, UAT coordination and release readiness.

What We're Looking For

Required

8+ years in business analysis on custom software, including leading a team or workstream.
A track record of results: turning vague requests into well-scoped solutions, and going beyond the job description to make things easier for stakeholders.
Excellent communication skills. You're confident leading demos and discovery with senior stakeholders and pushing back constructively.
Advanced, hands-on AI skills. AI has changed how you work.
A real instinct for user-centered design, and the judgment to shape AI-built prototypes into an experience users find easy.
Solid SQL, and comfort with relational data.

Preferred

Knowledge of US retirement plans (401(k), pooled employer plans, recordkeeping) or Financial Services.

What Success Looks Like

The business sees you as their go-to partner and trusts your judgment, even when you push back.
Developers rarely wait on requirements, and few defects reach the business.
Business partners spend less time on manual work because of what you build.
Within six months, you independently own the product area end to end.

Summary

The Senior Business Analyst will serve as a key liaison between business stakeholders and technology teams for Aon's Pooled Employer Plan (PEP) platform, a strategic solution supporting Aon's Retirement business. This role is responsible for understanding business objectives, identifying opportunities for platform enhancement, and translating business needs into actionable requirements, user stories, and delivery plans. The position will work closely with business leaders, developers, and product stakeholders to shape future platform capabilities and support ongoing modernization efforts. The ideal candidate will possess strong business analysis skills, excellent communication abilities, and experience leveraging modern tools and technologies, including AI-assisted analysis and requirements development, to accelerate solution delivery.

Key Responsibilities

Serve as a primary liaison between business stakeholders and technology teams for the PEP platform.
Facilitate discovery sessions, workshops, and solution discussions to understand business objectives and requirements.
Gather, analyze, and document business, functional, and process requirements.
Translate business needs into user stories, acceptance criteria, process flows, and delivery-ready requirements.
Partner closely with developers throughout the delivery lifecycle to clarify requirements and support successful implementation.
Leverage AI-assisted tools and techniques to accelerate requirements gathering, user story creation, documentation, and solution exploration.
Support backlog management, prioritization, release planning, and roadmap discussions.
Identify opportunities for process improvement, automation, and enhanced user experience.
Participate in testing, user acceptance activities, and validation of delivered functionality.
Assist with issue investigation, production support, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Create and maintain business and technical documentation.

Required Qualifications

8+ years of experience in Business Analysis, Product Analysis, or related technology delivery roles.
Strong experience gathering and documenting business and functional requirements.
Experience creating user stories, acceptance criteria, business process flows, and functional specifications.
Strong communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills.
Experience working directly with both business users and software development teams.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving abilities.
Experience supporting Agile delivery teams and backlog management activities.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting Retirement, Wealth Management, Financial Services, or similar business domains.
Experience working on product-oriented platforms or strategic technology initiatives.
Familiarity with software development, testing, and release management processes.
Experience working with web applications, APIs, and enterprise integrations.
Experience using AI-enabled tools to support business analysis, documentation, and requirements development.
Experience supporting cloud-based or modern SaaS applications.

Success Factors

Ability to translate business goals into actionable development work.
Strong partnership with business stakeholders and technology teams.
Effective use of AI and modern analysis techniques to improve delivery efficiency.
Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
Ability to contribute to the long-term growth and success of a strategic Aon Retirement platform.

HOW WE SUPPORT OUR COLLEAGUES

In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we are proud to be an equal opportunity workforce. At Aon, we believe a diverse workforce is an innovative workforce. Our agile, inclusive environment allows colleagues to manage their wellbeing and work/life balance while empowering you to be your authentic self.

Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging them to take time to focus on themselves. We offer a variety of workstyle options through our Smart Working model, but we also recognize that flexibility goes beyond just the place of work... and we are all for it!

Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips colleagues to learn, share and grow, helping them achieve their fullest potential. As a result, Aon colleagues are more connected, more relevant and more valued.

We are seeking an experienced Sr. Research Data Analyst to support health economics and health services research projects led by faculty in the Department of Health Policy and Management. The Sr. Research Data Analyst would contribute to a range of policy-relevant projects examining the health of older adults, mental health and substance use, value in the Medicare and Medicaid programs, health care affordability, and improving the value and quality of health care delivery. This is an ideal role for people hoping to apply for a PhD in health economics or health services research, or people with significant experience and interest in applied academic research.

The Sr. Research Data Analyst will primarily be responsible for constructing analytic datasets from large administrative databases including health insurance claims, electronic health records (EHRs), employment records, and population survey data. The position would involve developing analytic datasets, conducting data management and quality assessment, and applying statistical and econometric methods to support faculty-led research. In addition, the Sr. Research Data Analyst may also work with more unstructured data sources such as clinical notes or business ownership records.

Candidates with experience implementing econometric research designs—including instrumental variables and difference-in-differences—as well as regression modeling are especially encouraged to apply. The position provides opportunities to contribute intellectually to research projects and, when contributions warrant, to serve as a coauthor on resulting manuscripts.

Develop, manage, and maintain a database for study data for multiple studies.
Develop standard operating procedures for initial data entry and data updates.
Oversee quality control procedures for database and ongoing analysis.
Develop data models.
Conduct statistical analyses of data collected in this system to support empirical study.

Conduct data quality assessments and exploratory analyses using descriptive statistics, visualizations, and other diagnostic methods.

jobs.description:
Start Date: Immediate

JHNA, CTSi, and EXPANSIA have come together to form a Defense Technology platform focused on delivering high-impact technologies, technology-enabled services and advanced manufacturing solutions to the U.S. Department of Defense and related national security customers. Backed by Falfurrias Management Partners, the platform brings together deep domain expertise across Army, Navy, and Air Force and Space Force programs, digital engineering, systems integration, and specialized manufacturing capabilities.

The combined organization operates as a multi-entity aerospace and defense technology and tech-enabled services and manufacturing enterprise positioned for scalable growth, operational excellence, and long-term value creation.

Overview

Full-time

Location:
The ideal candidate will be local to the Tidewater/Newport News, VA area.

Aether Aerospace is currently seeking a Senior Operations Research and Systems Analysis (ORSA) to lead the analytical design, evaluation, and interpretation of modeling and simulation studies assessing military capabilities and mission outcomes over a six-month effort in support of a commercial client. The analyst will develop study methodologies, establish measures, design comparative cases, analyze simulation results, and translate findings into clear conclusions for customer decision-making. The position requires strong quantitative analysis skills and the ability to explain the significance and limitations of modeled results.

The analyst will work closely with the Study Lead, simulation technical staff, and operational subject matter experts. Operational SMEs will provide mission context and inform scenario assumptions; simulation technical staff will implement and execute scenarios. This position will establish analytical requirements and lead evaluation of the resulting data.

Responsibilities

Develop analysis plans identifying study questions, hypotheses, comparison cases, measures of effectiveness and performance, analytical methods, and criteria for interpreting results
Work with operational SMEs to translate customer objectives into defined scenarios, mission success criteria, and measurable outcomes
Establish consistent baselines and design controlled comparisons that isolate the effects of the capabilities being evaluated
Develop experimental designs, including replication strategies, sensitivity cases, and treatment of input uncertainty and observed run-to-run variability
Coordinate with simulation technical staff to define required inputs, output fields, event records, and data collection requirements
Assess whether model representations and available evidence support proposed measures; identify data gaps and outcomes that cannot be credibly estimated
Analyze mission completion time, mission success probability, personnel and platform losses, threat effectiveness, and resource expenditure where supported by the model and approved data
Distinguish modeled exposure, damage, mission kills, and casualties; prevent unsupported conversions between these outcomes
Evaluate uncertainty, convergence, and sensitivity to key assumptions and scenario conditions
Develop and maintain scripts and automated workflows to ingest, clean, validate, combine, and process simulation outputs; calculate study measures; and generate repeatable analytical summaries and visualizations using Python, R, MATLAB, Excel, or comparable tools
Support model verification and assessment of fitness for the intended analytical purpose, including review of pilot runs, anomalous results, and consistency across comparison cases
Maintain traceability from source data and assumptions through scenarios, simulation outputs, analytical findings, and conclusions
Prepare analytical reports, visualizations, and executive briefings that communicate results and their practical significance
Collaborate with operational SMEs to interpret the mechanisms driving favorable, neutral, and unfavorable outcomes
Support customer reviews, resolve analytical comments, and recommend further data collection or follow-on studies

Key Qualifications

Clearance:
Active Secret Clearance

Education & Years of Experience:
Bachelor’s degree in operations research, mathematics, statistics, engineering, systems analysis, or a related quantitative discipline. Ten or more years of relevant experience in operations research, quantitative systems analysis, mission effectiveness assessment, or modeling and simulation analysis. Equivalent combinations of advanced education and directly relevant experience will be considered.

Demonstrated experience designing and executing comparative studies using simulations or other quantitative analytical methods
Strong working knowledge of experimental design, statistical inference, uncertainty assessment, sensitivity analysis, and interpretation of repeated simulation runs
Proficiency with one or more analytical programming environments, such as Python, R, or MATLAB, and experience using Excel for analysis and reporting
Experience developing measures of effectiveness and performance tied to study objectives

OneFortyOne is seeking a Project Manager for a 12-month role based in our Richmond office to lead the delivery of our New Zealand Forest Information System, GIS and harvest forecasting advancement project. Own the project plan, coordinating scope, milestones, budget, resources and dependencies across the IT, forest information, GIS and harvest scheduling workstreams.

Digital Promise is a global nonprofit working to expand opportunity for every learner. We work with educators, researchers, technology leaders, and communities to design, investigate, and scale innovations that support learners. Our vision is that every person engages in powerful learning experiences that lead to a life of well-being, fulfillment, and economic mobility. For more information, visit the Digital Promise website and follow Digital Promise for updates.

About The Position

Digital Promise is seeking a highly organized, versatile Research Project Manager to join our

Networks and Programs team. This dual-function role acts as both the engine of our research

project operations and an active contributor to our research pipeline.

The Networks and Programs team acts as a catalyst for change and connects research, practice,

and innovation by building thriving networks of educators, bringing research into practice

through pilots, expanding our work globally, codifying proven ideas into replicable professional

services, and advancing collaborative, cross-sectoral conversations about the future of education.

This role will coordinate and support core research activities, including project planning,

deliverable tracking, data collection and analysis, and preparing results for publication. The

candidate should be skilled at working on multiple projects simultaneously and in working as a

member of interdisciplinary teams.

Exercise good judgment and ability in research and evaluation, with minimal guidance, to

define and carry out tasks and procedures, demonstrating understanding of larger project

contexts.

Understand and meet process and quality expectations, setting timelines and work plans

accordingly, which may include assigning tasks to others.

Choose and specify methods within work plans and approaches that advance equity

internally.

Monitor and report on completion of activities and progress toward project goals.
Anticipate issues and bring to the attention of project leaders, informing thes

consideration and development of solutions.

Project Management

Plan work sequentially and oversee daily operations across multiple projects, setting

timelines, assigning tasks, and tracking milestones to meet deadline and quality

expectations.

Proactively identify project bottlenecks, risks, or unexpected contingencies, working with

research leads to resolve issues efficiently.

publication of resources.

Coordinate team schedules, streamline communication channels, and manage logistics for

Develop, submit, and track IRB protocols and maintain IRB documentation.

Both independently and as a co-author, contribute to blogs, white papers, and other

education and/or the learning sciences, or equivalent experience in a related field.

Excellent writing, editing, communication, and interpersonal skills in multiple formats

Strong interpersonal and communication skills with impeccable attention to detail.
Proven ability to keep complex flows of work activity well-organized, productive, and on

track, including knowledge of project management tools. Familiarity with Salesforce,

Asana, Notion, Google Workspace, and/or Slack a plus.

Familiarity with the education and/or learning sciences research fields (cognitive

psychology, instructional science, education policy, educational data mining, educational

technology, AI, social science, etc.), including being conversant with the language of

research (e.g. research questions, populations, methods, analysis approaches, findings,

Ability to prioritize responsibilities, problem-solve and manage competing tasks,

deadlines, requirements, both independently and in a fast-paced team environment.

Ability to work flexibly and adaptively virtually and face-to-face with other team

members as program requirements change.

Creative, self-starter, multi-tasker, team player; strong work ethic, high standards,

Ability to travel as needed.
A passion for learning, a team mentality, creativity, and a positive “can-do” “yes-and”

The Impact You Will Have

Get customers to real intelligence outcomes fast. Ship a working v1 deployment and onboarding playbook within your first 30 days, using Claude to turn customer call recordings and account notes into tailored onboarding plans.
Turn early wins into habit. Use Claude and TRM's Intel platform to move analysts from one-off searches to recurring workflows, such as threat landscape and sector targeting, vulnerability prioritization, credential and infostealer exposure, ransomware readiness, and malware and IOC investigation.
Free your time for judgment work. Build production AI workflows that pull from Salesforce, Gong, and product usage telemetry to auto-generate account health summaries and QBR drafts.
Catch risk before renewal. Define adoption benchmarks across your portfolio (hands-on usage, workflow adoption, consumption, and account-specific success metrics) and use AI-generated health signals to flag at-risk accounts well before renewal decisions.
Prove value with executives. Run business reviews with CISOs, CTI directors, and security leaders, using AI-drafted summaries that tie product usage to outcomes they report on, such as faster investigations, reduced exposure, and analyst time saved.
Grow every account. Co-own renewal and expansion with the Account Director, carry NRR and GRR targets alongside Sales, and use AI to find the next workflow, team, or use case worth expanding into.
Shape the product. Use AI to cluster adoption blockers, feature gaps, data coverage needs, and new use cases into prioritized input for Product, and build the deployment tooling the next hire will inherit.

What We’re Looking For

5+ years in deployment strategy, onboarding, solutions engineering, customer success, or other post-sale roles, with proven ownership of NRR, GRR, and expansion metrics, and a record of using AI to scale that work.
Background in cyber threat intelligence, security operations, threat hunting, incident response, or a CTI vendor or platform environment (consulting, MSSP, and enterprise security teams all count).
Credibility with CTI practitioners: you understand how a corporate CTI team works (intelligence requirements, finished intelligence, handoffs to SOC and hunt teams), you're fluent in threat actors, MITRE ATT&CK, vulnerability and exploitation intelligence, ransomware, and stealer logs, and you use AI to sharpen that intelligence work and earn an analyst's trust in the first meeting.
Zero-to-one experience: you've built a deployment, onboarding, or customer success function or playbook from scratch, used AI to speed it up, and can point to the outcomes it produced.
Production AI fluency: you've built real, repeatable AI workflows (not just experiments) that synthesize data from multiple sources, and you can explain the data logic and where human judgment stays in the loop.
Executive presence: you can run a QBR with a CISO at a global bank or insurer and guide the room through substance, arriving prepared with AI-assisted briefs.
Experience supporting enterprise customers across North American time zones, including regulated industries such as financial services, insurance, telecom, and critical infrastructure, plus a bias to ship v1 before you have all the answers, with AI helping you move faster.
Nice to have: time at a threat intelligence vendor, an ISAC or ISAO, or a corporate intelligence team; familiarity with third-party and supply chain risk or cyber insurance workflows; certifications such as GCTI or GCIH.

About The Team

This team focuses on TRM's Intel platform, supporting CTI and security teams at enterprises facing sophisticated cyber threats.
You'd be the first Deployment Strategist dedicated to private sector CTI in North America, with high ownership, direct access to leadership, and real influence on how TRM deploys and retains customers in this segment. The work stretches you: you set the agenda in a function that doesn't exist yet.
The broader customer team works distributed, not distant: async-first communication in Slack, strong documentation, and intentional synchronous time for key decisions.
You'll work directly with the Head of Customer Success and the CRO, with close day-to-day collaboration with North America Sales and Product, built on trust and direct feedback.

Team Operating Rhythms

Distributed, not distant: we hold weekly customer syncs and biweekly health syncs, join POD calls, and regularly engage customers as trusted advisors.
Working hours and customer coverage align primarily with North American time zones, with flexibility to collaborate across regions when needed.
The team moves fast and iterates: v1 ships before it's perfect, and feedback is direct and specific.
Communication is async-first in Slack, with synchronous time reserved for customer work and key decisions.

Required Online And Collaboration Hours

Schedule: Primarily North American business hours, with occasional collaboration with customers outside US time zones if EMEA or APAC customers close earlier than expected.

On-Call Responsibilities

Schedule: No formal on-call rotation. As the primary lead for your customers, you see mission-critical issues through to resolution, including urgent customer needs outside standard hours when they arise.
Frequency: Not applicable (no rotation).

Travel Requirements

Schedule: Minimal. Most onboarding and enablement is virtual, with occasional travel to customers.
Frequency: About 10% of your time.

Onsite Requirements

Schedule: No regular onsite requirement. Occasional customer visits are covered under travel.
Frequency: Occasional, included in the 10% travel estimate.

Learn About TRM Speed In This Position

A working v1 deployment playbook within 30 days: built from your first 2 to 3 accounts, with measurable adoption benchmarks, and already used by the account team to set customer expectations.
A draft success metrics framework at 50% complete within 6 weeks, shared with the account team and key customers to validate direction before further investment.
The highest-impact expansion play scoped within 60 days: worked backward from renewal and expansion targets, with a concrete recommendation to leadership on which workflow or use case to prioritize and why, grounded in account data.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.
Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.
First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.
Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.
References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.
Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.
Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI Fluency Means You Are Among The Top 10 Percent Of Operators In Your Function In How You Apply AI To

Accelerate repeatable workflows
Structure and solve problems
Improve output quality
Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, You Should Expect

Priorities and targets to change quickly
Operating with a high degree of ambiguity
A high level of personal ownership and accountability
Close collaboration across teams and functions
Frequent, high-touch communication
Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking
A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.
Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.
Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

SUMMARY:
The Exchange Operations Program Manager is a senior level position that directs two case management teams supporting small business employers, employees, brokers and broker agents in the District.

Job Description

This position is located in the District of Columbia Health Benefit Exchange Authority. The mission of HBX is to implement a health care exchange program in the District of Columbia in accordance with the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (PPACA) of 2010 and the District of Columbia Health Benefit Exchange Authority Establishment Act of 2011, thereby ensuring access to quality and affordable health care to all District of Columbia residents.

This position is within the Partnerships and Marketplace Operations, Small Business Health Options Program (SHOP) team. The Exchange Operations Program Manager leads the SHOP Account Management and General Agency (GA) Relations teams. The Account Management team is responsible for providing tier two-level case management services to small businesses seeking to provide health and dental insurance to their employees through DC Health Benefit Exchange’s online marketplace, dchealthlink.com. The GA Relations team leads the agency’s engagement with brokers and general agency partners and provides case management services on behalf of their employer clients.

The Exchange Operations Program Manager is responsible for overseeing 2 supervisors and approximately 10 program analysts, case managers, and team leads tasked with assisting small businesses and their employees as they explore coverage options in the marketplace, including resolving technical issues that have an impact on enrollment. The Manager will also collaborate with the IT team at HBX on system development projects. The manager will support system operations and maintenance tasks, including the development and execution of test plans, and managing the tracking and resolution of system defects. In addition, the Manager serves as a liaison with Congressional benefits offices and is responsible for addressing policy and operational issues for Congressional employee enrollment. The manager is responsible for coordinating with internal stakeholders (HBX IT, EDI, Legal teams) and carrier partners to resolve escalated customer support cases. The Manager is responsible for setting the direction of the teams. The Manager is responsible for developing and managing performance goals so the teams are able to provide superior customer service to District businesses while improving processes, procedures, and systems changes to advance the agency’s administrative, managerial and operational efficiency. The manager will support initiatives focused on developing and strengthening the agency’s engagement with brokers and general agencies.

The Exchange Operations Program Manager must have knowledge of the Affordable Care Act, familiarity with the private health insurance market, extensive management experience, and demonstrated leadership skills. jobs.description:
About Baseten

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.

THE ROLE

Forward Deployed Engineering is Baseten’s swat team. We’re deeply technical, great with customers and fast, and we make the platform better with everything we learn in the field. FDEs take on the hardest inference problems for our most strategic customers: novel architectures, extreme scale, tight latency budgets. Then we turn those solutions into a platform no one can match.

We’re scaling the team quickly. We need someone to build the operating system that lets a fast-growing team of engineers stay focused on hard problems instead of coordination.

This is a high-visibility role with direct exposure to our largest customers and to company leadership. You’ll shape how a new kind of engineering team operates in the AI industry.

Responsibilities

Run the priority account cadence. Own the operating rhythm for our top accounts: daily hot-account check-ins, the weekly “forest view” review with leadership, and the account list itself with Sales leadership. Goal: zero surprise escalations to our execs.
Make the bridges work. Our FDE team connects to SA and Sales, Product, engineering (inference, infra), capacity and on-call. You’ll make sure each connection has a clear owner, cadence and SLA, with no hand-offs falling through the cracks:
Account transitions between solution architect and FDE, with exit criteria and runbooks
Non-P0 escalations to engineering teams, tracked and burned down weekly
Customer patterns and gaps flowing into the product roadmap

Drive cross-team programs for our largest customers. Coordinate multi-team efforts such as dedicated-capacity rollouts, cluster migrations, capacity reservations and large customer launches. Bring together various teams so these run on a plan, not on heroics.
Reduce toil and protect platform time. Track where engineering time goes: incidents another team owns, manual routing and config changes, after-hours pages. Work with engineering leads to remove the biggest sources of obstacles, so FDEs keep 30% of their time for shaping the platform.
Own the metrics. Build and report the metrics scorecard (account health, response times, toil, load per engineer, team health) to leadership.

Description

Amazon Key for Business (KfB) builds the technology that lets Amazon delivery associates and partners securely access multi-family buildings, gated communities, and commercial properties. Our systems power millions of secure deliveries by connecting Amazon's logistics network with building access hardware, property management platforms, and third-party smart locks around the world.

We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to drive cross-functional programs across our engineering, product, business development, and operations partners. You will own program execution end to end: defining scope with stakeholders, building the plan, identifying dependencies and risks early, and keeping a distributed set of engineering teams aligned on delivery. You will work on programs such as access hardware integrations, third-party lock partnerships, technician installation tooling, and access-security initiatives, in close partnership with product and engineering leaders.

This role is a strong fit for someone who enjoys turning ambiguity into a clear plan, is comfortable reading a design document and asking the right technical questions, and communicates crisply with audiences ranging from engineers to senior leadership.

Key job responsibilities

Own the end-to-end execution of cross-team technical programs, from requirements definition through launch and post-launch operations.
Partner with engineering managers and senior engineers to translate business requirements into technical scope, milestones, and delivery plans.
Identify dependencies, risks, and critical path items early; drive mitigation and escalate with clear options and recommendations.
Coordinate across engineering teams in multiple time zones, as well as product, business development, operations, security, and external partners.
Run program reviews and write clear, concise status updates, decision documents, and launch readiness assessments for leadership.
Establish and improve mechanisms for intake, prioritization, and release coordination so the team can deliver predictably as program volume grows.
Measure program outcomes against goals and drive continuous improvement in how the team plans and delivers.

A day in the life

You might start the day reviewing overnight progress from engineering teams in Europe and Asia, then run a working session with product and engineering to close open questions on a new partner integration. In the afternoon you update the program plan after a dependency shifted, write a short status note to leadership with the impact and your recommendation, and prepare for a launch readiness review later in the week.

About The Team

The KfB engineering organization is a globally distributed team of software development engineers, systems development engineers, and technical program managers across North America, Europe, and Asia. We own the backend services, device integrations, mobile applications, and internal tooling behind Amazon Key for Business. 2+ years of software development experience

new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Fleet Reliability
new_jobs.description:
About Tutor

We believe robots should be the next chapter in making physical labor safer and more affordable. But, nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t have a single robot. Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

We build robots that go straight into real factories and warehouses, to do real work, with real impact. Our robot Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Our robot Sonny does handwork, using two arms to achieve human-like dexterity in picking and packing. Every robot learns on the job, and each one we deploy makes the next one more capable, more affordable, and faster to put to work.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, we do it all in-house: the robotics hardware, the machine learning, and the field deployment and service. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

Why Tutor?

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

The Role

Tutor Intelligence robots run production on customer floors across North America. The fleet is growing faster than the tools behind it.

This role exists to fix that by building. The job is to find the parts of the operation that are held together with tape and replace them with something that works. Each project starts with a problem and very little else: no spec, no existing tool, no one to hand the work to. The person in this seat figures out what should exist, builds the first version, puts it in front of the people who need it, and keeps improving it until it runs on its own. Then it's on to the next one.

The role reports to the Head of Robot Operations and Reliability.

What The Work Looks Like

Most of what it takes to run a much larger fleet hasn't been built yet. This role builds it. That means looking at how the operation runs today, finding where it breaks or slows down, and building what should be there instead. The work is tools, data, and the way the work itself gets done.

The work will keep changing as the fleet grows. What stays the same is the job itself: see the problem, build the fix, put it to use, and keep improving it until it runs on its own.

The hard failures

Some robot failures don't make sense at first. A sensor tests fine on the bench and fails on the floor. A robot runs clean for three weeks and then stops every afternoon at 2:00. This role leads those investigations. That means pulling logs, reading field reports and parts history, talking to the technician who was there, building a theory, testing it, and staying with it until the cause is found and the fix holds.

Who This Is For

Someone who asks why a problem happened, not just how to make it stop, and who looks for the structure behind it: the process, the data, or the handoff that let it happen. Someone who, after watching a team struggle with the same problem twice, has already sketched a fix that keeps it from happening a third time, and built the first version. Someone who would rather own a result than report on one.

This can be an early-career role for someone with clear momentum, or a step up for someone five or more years in who is done reporting on problems they could have fixed. Either way, someone who learns fast, gets noticeably better every quarter, and wants the job to grow with the fleet.

Projects on the list

A training system that gives a field technician real-time instructions on the robot in front of them, built from what the fleet has already learned about that failure
Issue tracking that joins robot telemetry to what the technician saw on the floor, so an investigation goes from symptom to root cause and the fix can be checked across the fleet
Predictive tooling that flags a robot likely to fail before it does, from telemetry and parts history
Capacity planning for a regional network of technicians: where they should be based, how many, and how fast they need to reach a robot
The reliability data itself: what gets captured, how it connects, and which numbers are worth tracking

How The Work Gets Done

Code is a daily tool here, and so are AI agents. Build systems where agents pull the data, run the checks, and draft the write-ups, so the work runs without a person in the loop
Ship a rough first version early, put it in front of real users, and improve it from what they say
Work side by side with engineering, customer success and field technicians. Much of the best input comes from the people closest to the robots
When something finally works, write it down so the next person can run it without asking

Required

2-7 years as a technical program manager, industrial engineer, or engineer, or in operations or a similar technical role
A track record of building. At least one system, tool or program designed from scratch and put into real use, with a result that can be stated in numbers
Comfortable building software with AI coding tools and agents, or ready to pick it up fast. The language matters less than having shipped something that works
Clear thinking, and the ability to turn data into a clean picture that others can act on
Clear writing for engineers, customers and leadership
A degree in engineering or a technical field, or equivalent experience

Stands out

Has started something at a past job that didn't exist before, and it's still running
Experience in robotics, automation, manufacturing, logistics or fulfillment
Builds outside of work too: side projects, a home lab, something made just to see if it could be done

Probably Not The Right Fit For Someone Who

Prefers a clear task list and regular check-ins
Would rather maintain an existing system than build a new one
Wants the same week, every week

Why join

Few places hand one person this much ownership of how a fleet runs
What gets built here becomes how a robotics company runs its fleet
The role grows as the fleet grows

Benefits

Fully employer-covered health insurance, so you’re protected without the premium
A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future
Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees
Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year

Compensation

The base salary range for this role is $100,000 to $140,000, depending on experience.

Location and travel

In office in Watertown, MA. Travel to customer sites and regional teams as needed, roughly 10-25%.

To apply

Along with a résumé, send a short note about something you built: what the problem was, what you made, and what happened after. Links, photos and code are all welcome.

As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.

Experience conducting site investigations/characterizations, remedial investigations, feasibility studies, engineering evaluations, and remedial designs/actions.
Experience identifying and resolving key issues impacting remedy implementation (technical, regulatory, risk, stakeholder, land use, etc.) and emerging issues.

new_jobs.description:
Description

We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to own and drive AWS region expansion programs across the AWS Mission Networking family of services. You will enable dedicated network connectivity options for our U.S. National Security and Department of War customers to AWS Classified regions. You will also work with Defense Industrial Base (DIB) customers to support and expand Amazon's new launched AWS Secret Cloud for Industry (ASCI) service which enables dedicated connectivity to the AWS Secret Region for industry partners. You will build mechanisms and processes to automate and streamline the customer experience, working across AWS engineering, networking, and security teams to simplify access to the AWS classified (Secret and Top Secret) regions.

Are you energized by solving complex technical challenges that span multiple teams and systems? Do you thrive when turning ambiguity into clear plans and measurable outcomes? Amazon is looking for a Technical Program Manager to own and drive cross-functional programs that have considerable business impact. In this role, you will define program strategy, align stakeholders across engineering and business teams, and deliver results at scale. You will use your technical depth to question assumptions, assess architectural decisions, and ensure the right solutions ship on time. If you are a collaborative, data-driven problem solver who communicates with clarity and builds trust across all levels, we want to hear from you.

This position requires that the candidate selected be a US Citizen and must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph.

Key job responsibilities

Define and manage the lifecycle of complex cross-functional programs, setting clear objectives, success criteria, and roadmaps that align with organizational goals.
Drive alignment across business and technical stakeholders by facilitating crisp decision-making, providing context for technology choices, and prioritizing initiatives based on customer and business impact.
Identify and mitigate risks proactively by overseeing gaps between teams, processes, and system architectures, reducing exposure to common failure modes such as unclear requirements or insufficient testing.
Leverage your technical judgment to evaluate proposals, test assumptions, and make smart trade-offs between time, effort, and feature scope while partnering with engineering leaders to ensure solutions scale appropriately.
Communicate program progress and outcomes effectively through written narratives and executive presentations, building consensus when perspectives differ and escalating with good judgment when needed.
Partner with Business, Product, and Technology Leaders and teams to deliver value for our customers
Drive visibility and transparency of dates, milestones, and schedule throughout the customer onboarding process
Build inclusive relationships with partner groups in AWS Region Services, Networking and the World Wide Public Sector teams. Ensuring that these teams focus on our customers and support customer missions.

new_jobs.title: Senior Portfolio & Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Accelerate the possible by joining a winning Amcor team that’s transforming the packaging industry and improving lives around the world.

At Amcor, we unpack possibility through our innovative and responsible packaging to provide solutions that benefit our customers, our people and our planet. More than 10,000 consumers worldwide encounter our products every second and rely on us for safe access to food, medicine and other goods. We value their trust by making safety our guiding principle. It’s our core value and integral to how we do business.

Beyond this core principle, our shared values and behaviors unite us as we work together to elevate customers, shape lives and protect the future. We champion our customers and help them succeed. We play to win – adapting quickly in an everchanging world – and make smart choices to safeguard our business, our communities and the people we serve for generations to come. And we invest in our world-class team, empowering our colleagues to unpack their potential, because we believe when our people grow, so does our business.

To learn more about playing for Team Amcor, visit www.amcor.com I LinkedIn I Glassdoor I Facebook I YouTube

Job Description

Scope:

Portfolio & Project Manager is to oversee and coordinate our portfolio of projects in the region to ensure that the management process runs effectively and smoothly and that we deliver on the agreed metrics. This position requires excellent project management skills, and good communication to report at all levels in the organization. This role will help to drive consistency and standardization across global R&D project tools and practice with ongoing support for future R&D advancement projects.

About The Team

The R&D team
, composed of experienced professionals across multiple geographies, plays a critical role in advancing the company’s innovation and sustainability goals. Their focus spans three strategic pillars:

Sustainability
: Implement and scale sustainable business practices across operations, with a focus on reducing environmental impact, maximizing circularity, and enhancing long-term value creation. Product Innovation
: Design and develop new and improved packaging solutions that address evolving customer needs across diverse industries and applications. Cost Innovation
: Drive value creation by optimizing cost structures through material efficiency, process innovation, and design simplification—while maintaining or enhancing product performance and quality.

This role is pivotal in supporting the Global R&D organization to shape the future of rigid packaging by delivering transformative solutions that meet evolving customer expectations, regulatory demands, and environmental imperatives.

Key Function Responsibilities

Portfolio Management:
Develop and maintain a comprehensive portfolio of projects, ensuring alignment with the company’s strategic goals.
Prioritize projects based on business impact, resource availability, and market demands.
Monitor and report on portfolio performance, providing insights and recommendations for improvements and filling business gaps.
Support the team in gathering metrics and systems to enable consistent data collection and alignment across global teams, driving standardization of dashboards and reporting.
Secure use and understanding of the Portfolio Management Process and set up the training needed for your regions, working with the R&D Operations PPM

Project Planning and Execution:
Lead implementation and maintenance of stage gate process with clear governance implemented across all functions along with the tools required for the work to be executed.
Support the team with planning, execution, and delivery of projects within the portfolio,
ensuring they are completed on time, within scope, risk management and within budget.
Coordinate cross-functional teams, including product development, supply chain, sales and finance, to achieve project prioritization and execution.
Identify and mitigate risks, resolving issues promptly to keep projects on track.
Implement best practices in project and portfolio management, driving continuous improvement in processes and methodologies.
Stay updated with industry trends and advancements, incorporating relevant innovations into project management practices.

Resource Management:
Engage with key stakeholders, including senior management, clients, and partners, to ensure alignment and support for projects, programs and portfolios.
Communicate project status, milestones, and outcomes effectively to all stakeholders.
Together with the Regional PPM Director, ensure that the NA and LATAM associated project teams follow the ways of work defined to drive growth & improvement.
Organize and lead cross functional teams to implement projects from initial concept to successful completion following Amcor’s standard stage-gate process focusing on speed to market, development efficiency, cost, business continuity, quality and on time delivery.

Key Performance Indicators

Innovation and Renovation Pipeline:
Portfolio Alignment Score: % of projects aligned with global product strategy, sustainability goals, and market differentiation.
Project Timing: The average time taken to develop a new product or service from concept to market launch. (Speed to Market)
On-Time Project Delivery: % of R&D projects completed within their originally scheduled timelines, reflecting the efficiency of the R&D process.
Budget Adherence: % of projects delivered within approved budget.
Project Compliance: % of focus initiatives in the Green or Amber range for health

Return on Innovation Investment (ROI):
Innovation financial Net Project Value: the R&D value given to the projects in our portfolio to ensure we are assigning our resources to the proper projects (R&D Timing, Investment, Revenue calculations)
Stakeholder Satisfaction: feedback from your key stakeholders on performance

Tools & Capabilities:
Project Measurements: measurable improvements in project time, cost and throughput
Standardization Rate: Measures the percentage of processes, tools, and methodologies that have been standardized across all R&D teams globally.

Qualifications

Degree in Business Administration, Project Management, Engineering, or a related field. Master’s degree or Project Management or certification is a plus.
Expertise in project management software and tools desired.
Proven experience in portfolio and project management, preferably in the packaging or manufacturing industry.
Strong understanding of project management methodologies (e.g., Agile, Waterfall, Scrum).
Good communication, and interpersonal skills.
Ability to work effectively in a global, multicultural and matrix organization. Also, must be fluent in English and Spanish.
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision
Experience with MS Office, SharePoint, MS Project, and SAP preferred
Familiarity with Wrike and Power BI is a plus.

Our Expectations

We Expect Our People To Be Guided By The Amcor Way And Demonstrate Our Values Every Day To Enable The Business To Win. We Are Winning When

Our people are engaged and developing as part of a high-performing Amcor team
Our customers grow and prosper from Amcor’s quality, service, and innovation
Our investors benefit from Amcor’s consistent growth and superior returns
The environment is better off because of Amcor’s leadership and products

Equal Opportunity Employer/Minorities/Females/Disabled/Veterans/Sexual Orientation/Gender Identity

If you would like more information about your EEO rights as an applicant under the law, please click on the "Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal" Poster . If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please call 224-313-7000 and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information.

E-Verify

We verify the identity and employment authorization of individuals hired for employment in the United States.

Benefits

When you join Amcor, you will have access to a comprehensive benefits and compensation package that includes:

Medical, dental and vision plans
Flexible time off, starting at 80 hours paid time per year for full-time salaried employees
Company-paid holidays starting at 8 days per year and may vary by location
Wellbeing program & Employee Assistance Program
Health Savings Account/Flexible Spending Account
Life insurance, AD&D, short-term & long-term disability, and voluntary benefits
Paid Parental Leave
Retirement Savings Plan with company match

Discretionary annual bonus program (initial eligibility dependent upon hire date)

new_jobs.title: Acquisition Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Title

Acquisition Program Manager

At KBR, we deliver science, technology and engineering solutions to governments and companies around the world. KBR employs approximately 37,000 people worldwide with customers in more than 85 countries and operations in over 28 countries. KBR is proud to work with its customers across the globe to provide technology, value-added services, and long-term operations and maintenance services to ensure consistent delivery with predictable results.

Trinzic is the future independent company to be created through the planned spin-off of KBR's Mission Technology Solutions business, expected in January 2027. Our people work at the frontier of what is possible, delivering solutions in challenging environments and advancing some of the world's highest-priority national security and space missions. 

Backed by decades of mission success, deep expertise, and trusted partnerships, Trinzic will launch as a global organization with more than 18,000 employees supporting customers around the world. Join us at a defining moment and help shape the future of a company built to tackle complex challenges and make a meaningful impact. 

Candidates who join KBR's Mission Technology Solutions business before the spin-off will transition to Trinzic when the separation is complete and will not need to reapply for employment. 

KBR/Trinzic is seeking an Acquisition Program Manager to join our team. This position supports the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Mobility and Training Aircraft Directorate, C-130 Hercules Division (AFLCMC/WLN). This is a full-time position located at Robins AFB.

Key Responsibilities

Developing program documentation to support Request for Proposal, Milestone Decisions and Acquisition Strategy
Provide technical analysis integration of such aspects of program management as engineering, procurement, financial management, environmental management, configuration
Ensure program requirements and statements of work capture and are planned to the level of detail required for execution.
Develop requirements, Milestone documentation, and provide technical writing expertise for deliverables
Participate in an advisory role to conduct analysis, draft, and deliver source selection evaluation inputs
Provide recommendations to ensure project information integrates into existing program strategy
Employ integration, communication, coordination, organizational, and planning expertise to technical and acquisition efforts across numerous functional disciplines
Perform a range of program management activities such as gathering a variety of program information; conducting analyses; developing program strategies; milestone planning, tracking, and scheduling; establishing and maintaining databases
Analyze program activities such as acquisition program planning, financial management, cost analysis, management techniques, or documentation requirements
Compile and review budgets against actual performance to control budgets and provide for proper financial decisions
Aid in developing and implementing strategies to achieve program objectives safely and within agreed time, cost, technical, quality and other performance criteria. Products generally include acquisition strategies/plans, other statutory/regulatory documentation (writing, editing, cross-walking, and compliance checking), briefings and white papers supporting acquisition decisions at each phase or milestone of the Acquisition life cycle
Participate in the preparation of budgets and schedules and perform/assist in financial analyses such as funding profiles, outlook, and variance analysis
Develop plans including budgets and schedules to meet program/project. Support the customer PM in executing his/her mission as single point of integrative responsibility needed to ensure that everything in the program is managed effectively to ensure a successful project outcome
Support customer PM in program progress reviews and other performance reviews. Assist in creating/briefing higher level executive agency system acquisition or program summary reports
Demonstrate advanced expertise in DoD, Agency, and/or industry standards and engineering requirements. Advise colleagues on interpretation of standards within the context of program objectives.

Work Environment

Location: On-site, Warner-Robins AFB, GA
Travel Requirements: Minimal 0-20%
Working Hours: Standard

Required Qualifications

Bachelors degree in Business or relevant technical discipline and 4-7 years of relevant program management experience managing DoD multi-year production, sustainment, or modernization contracts
Clearance: SECRET security clearance is required
Proficient in Microsoft Office 365 applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, Outlook, and SharePoint, for data analysis, reporting, collaboration, and executive-level presentations.
Possesses exceptional written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to brief senior leadership, engage stakeholders across multiple organizations, and develop clear, concise logistics plans, technical documentation, and program reports.

new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

Addepar is a global data and AI platform empowering investment professionals to turn complex financial information into actionable intelligence. Addepar unifies portfolio, market and client data in a total portfolio view and delivers AI-powered insights within investment and client workflows. More than 1,500 firms in 60 countries use Addepar to manage and advise on nearly $10 trillion in assets. Its open platform integrates with 650 software, data and consulting partners to power end-to-end investment operations across firms of all sizes and levels of complexity. Addepar supports clients worldwide with offices in New York City, Salt Lake City, São Paulo, London, Edinburgh, Geneva, Warsaw, Dubai, Pune and Singapore.

The Role

We are currently seeking a Sr. Manager, Security Operations to lead our Global Security Operations team within Addepar’s Information Security & Risk organization. In this role, you will own the day-to-day running of our detection and response function, act as incident commander for security incidents, and partner with our 24/7 MSSP to ensure threats are identified and handled quickly. You will set the operational objectives and strategy for Security Operations, lead and grow a global team, and shape our detection strategy for threats specific to Addepar’s environment. Beyond the immediate response, you will make sure we learn from every incident by driving post-incident follow-through, turning incident trends into lasting fixes with partners across the business, and reporting on the health of the program to Security leadership. We also want this leader to modernize how Security Operations works, applying AI and automation (AIOps) to speed up triage, investigation and response so the team can focus on the highest-impact work. The successful candidate is a hands-on leader who brings structure, calm and accountability to high-pressure situations.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States for any employer without requiring current or future visa sponsorship (for example, employment-based visas such as H-1B, F-1/OPT, or similar), and must be authorized to begin work in the U.S. on their first day of employment.

What You’ll Do

Operational Leadership: Lead the day-to-day operations of Addepar’s Global Security Operations team, and serve as incident commander for major security incidents
People Management: Manage and develop a globally distributed team. Provide mentorship and training, set the team’s roadmap and OKRs, and manage on-call coverage across time zones
MSSP Partnership: Own the relationship with our 24/7 Managed Security Services Provider (MSSP), including escalation paths, service quality, vendor performance and cost, and handoffs to the internal team
Detection & SIEM: Own our detection strategy and the health of our SIEM environment. This includes building custom detections for threats unique to Addepar, tuning alerts to improve fidelity and reduce noise, expanding log source coverage, and ensuring the platform scales as Addepar grows
AI-Driven Modernization: Lead the modernization of our SecOps function through AIOps, using AI and automation to streamline alert triage, enrichment, investigation and response, reduce manual toil, and scale the team’s impact
Documentation & Playbooks: Build and own our incident response documentation, including playbooks, runbooks and training materials, and keep it current as threats and our environment evolve
Post-Incident Accountability: Maintain our post-incident process so action items are clearly owned, tracked and closed across teams, covering both immediate fixes and longer-term improvements
Root Cause Remediation: Use incident trends to identify recurring root causes, and partner with Engineering, Infrastructure, Security and Product teams to prioritize and deliver preventive fixes
Metrics, KPIs & Reporting: Define and track key SecOps metrics and KPIs, and present a holistic monthly view of the Security Operations function to senior leadership
Security Awareness: Champion security awareness across the company through tabletop exercises, training sessions and talks
On-Call: Participate in a global on-call rotation, including responding to critical security events outside of standard working hours

Who You Are

You have 8+ years of experience in security operations, detection engineering, or incident response
You have 3+ years of people management experience, with a track record of mentoring and developing security teams
You have proven experience as an incident commander for security incidents: leading the response, coordinating multiple workstreams, running postmortems and driving action items to completion
You have hands-on experience with Amazon Web Services (AWS), including investigating and responding to security events in the cloud
You hold a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Cyber Security, or a related field, or have equivalent experience
You communicate clearly with technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership, and can influence peers and leaders to build agreement in sensitive situations
You bring structure to ambiguous, fast-moving situations and stay composed under pressure

Job Description

Scope:

Portfolio & Project Manager is to oversee and coordinate our portfolio of projects in the region to ensure that the management process runs effectively and smoothly and that we deliver on the agreed metrics. This position requires excellent project management skills, and good communication to report at all levels in the organization. This role will help to drive consistency and standardization across global R&D project tools and practice with ongoing support for future R&D advancement projects.

About The Team

The R&D team
, composed of experienced professionals across multiple geographies, plays a critical role in advancing the company’s innovation and sustainability goals. Their focus spans three strategic pillars:

Sustainability
: Implement and scale sustainable business practices across operations, with a focus on reducing environmental impact, maximizing circularity, and enhancing long-term value creation. Product Innovation
: Design and develop new and improved packaging solutions that address evolving customer needs across diverse industries and applications. Cost Innovation
: Drive value creation by optimizing cost structures through material efficiency, process innovation, and design simplification—while maintaining or enhancing product performance and quality.

This role is pivotal in supporting the Global R&D organization to shape the future of rigid packaging by delivering transformative solutions that meet evolving customer expectations, regulatory demands, and environmental imperatives.

Key Function Responsibilities

Portfolio Management:
Develop and maintain a comprehensive portfolio of projects, ensuring alignment with the company’s strategic goals.
Prioritize projects based on business impact, resource availability, and market demands.
Monitor and report on portfolio performance, providing insights and recommendations for improvements and filling business gaps.
Support the team in gathering metrics and systems to enable consistent data collection and alignment across global teams, driving standardization of dashboards and reporting.
Secure use and understanding of the Portfolio Management Process and set up the training needed for your regions, working with the R&D Operations PPM

Project Planning and Execution:
Lead implementation and maintenance of stage gate process with clear governance implemented across all functions along with the tools required for the work to be executed.
Support the team with planning, execution, and delivery of projects within the portfolio,
ensuring they are completed on time, within scope, risk management and within budget.
Coordinate cross-functional teams, including product development, supply chain, sales and finance, to achieve project prioritization and execution.
Identify and mitigate risks, resolving issues promptly to keep projects on track.
Implement best practices in project and portfolio management, driving continuous improvement in processes and methodologies.
Stay updated with industry trends and advancements, incorporating relevant innovations into project management practices.

Resource Management:
Engage with key stakeholders, including senior management, clients, and partners, to ensure alignment and support for projects, programs and portfolios.
Communicate project status, milestones, and outcomes effectively to all stakeholders.
Together with the Regional PPM Director, ensure that the NA and LATAM associated project teams follow the ways of work defined to drive growth & improvement.
Organize and lead cross functional teams to implement projects from initial concept to successful completion following Amcor’s standard stage-gate process focusing on speed to market, development efficiency, cost, business continuity, quality and on time delivery.

Key Performance Indicators

Innovation and Renovation Pipeline:
Portfolio Alignment Score: % of projects aligned with global product strategy, sustainability goals, and market differentiation.
Project Timing: The average time taken to develop a new product or service from concept to market launch. (Speed to Market)
On-Time Project Delivery: % of R&D projects completed within their originally scheduled timelines, reflecting the efficiency of the R&D process.
Budget Adherence: % of projects delivered within approved budget.
Project Compliance: % of focus initiatives in the Green or Amber range for health

Return on Innovation Investment (ROI):
Innovation financial Net Project Value: the R&D value given to the projects in our portfolio to ensure we are assigning our resources to the proper projects (R&D Timing, Investment, Revenue calculations)
Stakeholder Satisfaction: feedback from your key stakeholders on performance

Tools & Capabilities:
Project Measurements: measurable improvements in project time, cost and throughput
Standardization Rate: Measures the percentage of processes, tools, and methodologies that have been standardized across all R&D teams globally.

Qualifications

Degree in Business Administration, Project Management, Engineering, or a related field. Master’s degree or Project Management or certification is a plus.
Expertise in project management software and tools desired.
Proven experience in portfolio and project management, preferably in the packaging or manufacturing industry.
Strong understanding of project management methodologies (e.g., Agile, Waterfall, Scrum).
Good communication, and interpersonal skills.
Ability to work effectively in a global, multicultural and matrix organization. Also, must be fluent in English and Spanish.
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision
Experience with MS Office, SharePoint, MS Project, and SAP preferred
Familiarity with Wrike and Power BI is a plus.

We Expect Our People To Be Guided By The Amcor Way And Demonstrate Our Values Every Day To Enable The Business To Win. We Are Winning When

Our people are engaged and developing as part of a high-performing Amcor team
Our customers grow and prosper from Amcor’s quality, service, and innovation
